subject: Social Studies
stem: India follows a 'mixed economy', which means:

options.option_text: Both public (government) and private sectors coexist and contribute to economic activity
Only the government controls all economic activity
Only private individuals control all economic activity with zero government role
Barter is the only method of exchange used

explanation: A mixed economy combines elements of both public (state-owned) and private enterprise — India's post-independence economic model, distinct from purely socialist or purely capitalist systems.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Inflation refers to a situation in an economy where there is:

options.option_text: A general, sustained rise in the price level of goods and services
A general fall in prices across the economy
No change in prices at all
A rise in prices of only one single product

explanation: Inflation is a sustained, economy-wide rise in the general price level, reducing the purchasing power of money over time. A fall in prices is deflation.

subject: Social Studies
stem: India's First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) primarily focused on:
explanation: The First Five-Year Plan prioritised agriculture and irrigation (including dam projects), given post-independence food security concerns. The Second Plan (Mahalanobis model) later emphasised heavy industry.
